narration.text: Goalkeepers used to pick up every back pass.
The 1990 World Cup was criticised as dull and defensive.
Defenders passed back, keepers held the ball, and time drained away.
So in 1992, the rule changed.
If a teammate kicks it back on purpose, the goalkeeper cannot use his hands.
It was made to stop time-wasting. Every goal has a story.

facts.claim: The back-pass rule was introduced in 1992.
facts.quote: The back-pass rule was introduced in 1992 to discourage time-wasting and unduly defensive play after the 1990 World Cup was widely criticised as excessively dull, rife with back-passing and goalkeepers holding up the ball to waste time.

facts.claim: It was brought in to discourage time-wasting and overly defensive play.
facts.quote: The back-pass rule was introduced in 1992 to discourage time-wasting and unduly defensive play after the 1990 World Cup was widely criticised as excessively dull, rife with back-passing and goalkeepers holding up the ball to waste time.

facts.claim: The 1990 World Cup was criticised for dull and defensive play.
facts.quote: Daniel Jeandupeux, then the manager of Ligue 1 team Caen, proposed the rule in December 1990 in a letter to the FIFA technical committee after analysing data from Ligue 1 goalkeepers.

facts.claim: A goalkeeper may not handle the ball after a teammate deliberately kicks it to him.
facts.quote: However, the back-pass rule prohibits goalkeepers from handling the ball after it has been deliberately kicked to them by a team-mate or directly after a throw-in taken by a team-mate.
